hero.headline: JetBlue ending direct flights from Vero Beach to New York JFK in September
hero.teaser: JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airlin
hero.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end September 9, just nine months after the route began operating. JetBlue told WPTV that demand for the new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped. The carrier will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route, and all affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. The optimism surrounding the launch contrasted sharply with the route's short lifespan, as the service failed to attract sufficient passenger numbers to remain viable.

Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. The Boston service remains operational and provides ongoing connectivity for the region. However, the loss of the JFK route represents a setback for efforts to increase air service options at the smaller regional airport. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline's statement indicated that all affected customers would receive full refunds for their cancelled flights as the carrier winds down operations on the route over the coming weeks. The decision to discontinue the JFK service comes as airlines continue to evaluate route profitability and adjust their schedules based on passenger demand patterns.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up traffic enforcement after deputies clock drivers at 105 mph
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break and placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern.

Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said she recently had someone pass her on Interstate 95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues said he stopped a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road, got someone going 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1, and clocked his top speed on Indian River Drive at 73 mph, where the posted limit is 25 mph. Benning said the county sees a lot of excessive speeding.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155 percent increase.

Del Toro said he has a family that drives on these roadways and cares about his loved ones and everyone else's loved ones, adding that he wants to make this a safer community. Residents described the danger they encounter daily on local roads. Ashley, a St. Lucie County resident, said nobody slows down and called the situation insane. Jessica, another local driver, said drivers are careless and cut people off. Del Toro characterized the stepped-up enforcement as addressing a quality of life issue for the community.

cards.headline: Donalds holds commanding lead as Florida governor primary enters final stretch
cards.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly have emerged as frontrunners in Florida's governor race as the primary approaches. Donalds holds a commanding advantage in Republican polling and fundraising, while Jolly has consolidated support in the Democratic contest. The closing weeks are bringing new attacks, a ballot challenge and questions about the candidates' vulnerabilities heading toward November.

A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48% among Republican voters, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8% and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds has announced more than $90 million raised across his campaign operation, with President Donald Trump endorsing him. Collins, who Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed lieutenant governor in August 2025, has not received an endorsement from DeSantis. During a Thursday campaign call, Collins positioned himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds and urged Renner to leave the race, saying it is a two-person race between himself and Donalds.

Fishback faces pressure on two fronts. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. Fishback denies being antisemitic. Collins is also challenging Fishback's candidacy, alleging he lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee. Because ballots have already been printed, a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents.

On the Democratic side, Jolly addressed his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit that managed trust funds for people with disabilities. The indictment alleges the scheme operated from 2009 through 2025. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress. In a campaign video, Jolly said he had no knowledge of the alleged theft. A June Change Research survey commissioned by Freedom Project USA, a group aligned with Democrats, showed Jolly leading Donalds 47% to 42% among registered voters and 49% to 43% among likely voters.

cards.headline: Court hearing scheduled on challenge to Fishback's gubernatorial eligibility
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback faces a ballot challenge alleging he does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors.
cards.body:
Lt. Gov. Jay Collins is challenging the candidacy of Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee to address the eligibility challenge. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. Because ballots have already been printed for the July 18 primary, the judge said a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots.

The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Fishback denies being antisemitic and says the spending shows Republican establishment figures are concerned about his campaign. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Fishback at 8% support in the Republican gubernatorial primary, behind U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds at 48% and Collins at 9%.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.body:
Demolition has begun at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay.

Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. The tornadoes destroyed buildings 18, 10, and 9 at the school. Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, explained how the hurricane damage merged with existing plans. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," Gernaine said. "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on."

The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027. The project combines planned improvements that were already scheduled with the necessary repairs from the hurricane damage.

The reconstruction effort represents a significant investment in the school's infrastructure, modernizing facilities that were due for upgrades while also replacing the structures lost to the Hurricane Milton tornadoes. The combination of planned construction and storm damage repairs allows the district to comprehensively address both immediate needs and long-term facility improvements in a single project timeline.

cards.headline: JetBlue ending direct flights from Vero Beach to JFK Airport in September
cards.teaser: JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December.
cards.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue said in a statement to WPTV that demand for this new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped. JetBlue will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route and has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

cards.headline: Clearwater financier Leo Govoni faces federal charges in $100 million theft scheme
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors allege Leo Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit that managed trust funds for people with disabilities and other special needs.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors have charged Clearwater financier Leo Govoni and accountant John Witeck with stealing more than $100 million from a nonprofit that managed trust funds for people with disabilities and other special needs. The indictment alleges the scheme operated from 2009 through 2025 and involved fraudulent account statements and transfers through Govoni-controlled companies. Govoni and Witeck have been charged in the case.

Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress. Govoni supported Jolly's past political campaigns and served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. Donalds supporters have circulated opposition research emphasizing those connections, including that Jolly and his wife worked for Govoni-linked companies, Govoni raised money for Jolly's campaigns, and Jolly later employed Govoni's son in Congress. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. In a campaign video, Jolly said he had no knowledge of the alleged theft and welcomed scrutiny of his record. Jolly said that unlike too many politicians today who hide behind lawyers or refuse to answer questions, he is an open book, because when you have done nothing wrong, you have nothing to hide.

hero.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast seeks fosters and adopters during shelter renovation
hero.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation.
hero.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation. The construction will modernize the shelter, improve animal living spaces, enhance adoption areas, and create more comfortable and visible spaces to care for animals. The renovation presents significant challenges for the animals, who are being held in smaller spaces during the work.

Sarah Fisher of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast said the animals are really being affected by the sound of the construction. It's very loud and the sound being in a closed kennel can be very stressful for an animal, Fisher said. About 50 animals are currently in foster care, but the shelter is hoping to get the remaining 67 animals housed on-site either fostered or adopted, with most of them being dogs. The shelter continues to receive animals daily and is on a mission to get them out as quickly as they come in.

hero.headline: Florida Panthers announce 2026-27 regular season schedule with home opener in October
hero.teaser: The Florida Panthers will open the 2026-27 NHL season on the road against the Stanley Cup Champion Carolina Hurricanes on September 29 before returning for their home opener on October 11.
hero.body:
The Florida Panthers will begin their 2026-27 NHL regular season on the road against four Western Conference opponents. The team opens against the Carolina Hurricanes, the 2026 Stanley Cup Champion, on Sept. 29 in a marquee matchup to start the year. The road trip continues with a stop in San Jose on Oct. 6. After completing their four-game road swing, the Panthers will return to South Florida for their home opener on Saturday, Oct. 11, when they welcome the Minnesota Wild to Amerant Bank Arena.

December will be particularly busy for the Panthers with seven home games scheduled, including four special holiday matchups to close out 2026. The final home game of the calendar year is set for Dec. 30 against the Buffalo Sabres. The team has planned two consecutive five-game homestands during the season. The first homestand will run from Dec. 19-30, and the second is scheduled from March 2-12.

cards.headline: Miami Heat introduce Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis Jr. at Kaseya Center
cards.teaser: The Miami Heat officially introduced two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo and forward Bobby Portis Jr. at the Kaseya Center on Thursday, with both players receiving standing ovations from fans.
cards.body:
Loud chants of 'Giannis' filled the Kaseya Center on Thursday afternoon as the Miami Heat introduced Antetokounmpo and Portis to South Florida. Head Coach Erik Spoelstra confirmed that Heat President Pat Riley asked him if he wanted to coach Antetokounmpo, to which he responded yes. Antetokounmpo, standing 6'11 and weighing 240 pounds, comes to Miami after back-to-back injury-filled seasons.

Antetokounmpo said he thrives on pressure and needs it at this point in his career to reach the next level. The two-time MVP, NBA champion and Finals MVP said he feels he accomplishes whatever he sets his mind to and believes Miami is the best route to winning more championships. He emphasized he is not focused on measurables but on how many championships he can help bring to the franchise.

Portis, who has been coming off the bench throughout his career as a sixth man, said he prides himself on working every day in the summer to get better and plans to remain aggressive in Miami. He has played with Antetokounmpo for six years and said his relationship with Bam Adebayo has been built off being competitors. Spoelstra said the squad will play a lot of positionless basketball with Antetokounmpo, Portis and Adebayo on the floor together.

cards.headline: Argentina defeats England 2-1 in World Cup semifinal with late goals
cards.teaser: Argentina rallied from a 1-0 deficit with goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday and advance to the World Cup final.
cards.body:
Trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute, Argentina rallied for a 2-1 victory over England on Wednesday with goals from Enzo Fernandez and substitute Lautaro Martinez. Anthony Gordon scored the opening goal for England in the 55th minute. Messi fed the ball to Fernandez to sweep in the equalizer from outside the box in the 85th minute, and two minutes into stoppage time, Messi sent in a cross for Martinez to head in the winner. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves while Mac Allister sent a header off the post as wave after wave of Argentina attacks came. Martinez said he told teammate Alexis Mac Allister before the match that he was going to score and win it.

The defending champions will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The loss for England marks the third time the team has come up short in the World Cup semifinals after losses to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018. England captain Harry Kane said he was gutted for the team, the staff, and the fans after falling short. England coach Thomas Tuchel said Argentina played with more risk and rhythm while his team played with the feeling they had a lot to lose. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the game was a show of the collectiveness and brotherhood of the team, saying they were ready to leave everything on the pitch.

cards.headline: Spain advances to World Cup final with 2-0 victory over France
cards.teaser: Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot and Pedro Porro added another goal as Spain defeated France 2-0 on Tuesday to reach its first World Cup final since 2010.
cards.body:
Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot in the 22nd minute after Lamine Yamal drew a foul when kicked by defender Lucas Digne in the penalty area. After a poor first touch with his head, Digne was trying to clear the ball when Yamal raced in from behind to challenge. The ball hit off the elbow of the leaping teen before he was kicked by Digne, who was playing in his 63rd game for France only six days before his 33rd birthday. Oyarzabal's fifth goal of this year's World Cup was his 30th goal in 60 international games for Spain. Pedro Porro added another goal on a give-and-go with Dani Olmo in the 58th minute to put Spain up 2-0.

A day after his 19th birthday, Yamal was denied a goal on a close offside call that came soon after Porro's strike. Spain will face either defending champion Argentina or England on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The win marked the third summer in a row that Spain beat France in a tournament semifinal match. Yamal scored in a 2-1 win in the 2024 European Championship semifinals just days before his 17th birthday, and Spain won 5-4 in Nations League play last year. France will play in the third-place game in Miami Gardens, Florida, on Saturday.

cards.headline: Atlanta increases security for England-Argentina World Cup semifinal
cards.teaser: Atlanta police announced increased personnel and resources for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal match, considered one of the tournament's highest-risk games due to longstanding tensions between the two nations.
cards.body:
Security and police presence will be increased for Wednesday's England-Argentina World Cup semifinal match in Atlanta. The matchup is considered one of the tournament's highest-risk games because of longstanding tensions between the two nations stemming from the 1982 Falklands War. Videos circulating online appear to show England and Argentina fans clashing in Miami, where England played Norway over the weekend. Atlanta police said additional personnel and resources are already in place and will continue to be strategically assigned in and around event venues for Wednesday's match.

Argentina is the defending champion, while England has not won a World Cup since 1966. It is also the first time since England's World Cup win in 1966 that its national team has earned a berth in the semifinals. In addition to claiming three World Cup titles, Argentina has been the tournament's runner-up twice.

cards.headline: England and Argentina renew fierce World Cup rivalry in semifinal
cards.teaser: England and Argentina meet in Atlanta on Wednesday in a World Cup semifinal that resumes one of the fiercest rivalries in international soccer, with the winner advancing to face Spain in the final.
cards.body:
England and Argentina will meet in the World Cup semifinals on Wednesday in Atlanta, resuming one of international soccer's fiercest rivalries. The World Cup rivalry between the nations dates back to 1962, but intensified after England's 1-0 quarterfinal win in 1966 when Argentina captain Antonio Rattin, whose death was announced on Saturday, was sent off in a bad-tempered match. Twenty years later in Mexico, Diego Maradona scored the infamous Hand of God goal that helped Argentina to a 2-1 quarterfinal win. That same game saw Maradona score what many believe to be the greatest World Cup goal ever when he dribbled the ball from the halfway line before beating England goalkeeper Peter Shilton. England felt aggrieved again in 1998 when David Beckham was sent off for kicking out at Argentina midfielder Diego Simeone before losing on penalties. Beckham scored a penalty in a 1-0 win four years later that contributed to Argentina being eliminated at the group stage.

England coach Thomas Tuchel said the two shirts are iconic and the historic matches are iconic, but as a coach he treats it as just another football match. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said Maradona's goal will be forever in their hearts and anybody who loves football will remember that in the best way possible. The winner will play Spain in the final in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts earn top 15 finish at nationals, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month, qualifying them for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine each came to gymnastics through different paths but now compete as one unit. Rose-Daris said she was drawn to the sport because she knew how to do a cartwheel. Supan said she was inspired by watching gymnasts on YouTube and how amazing they are and how fun it looks. Rine said she loves gymnastics because she learns new things.

Head Coach Candice Lazuka said the team had a really good season, competing locally, traveling, and advancing to states and regionals. At nationals, the gymnasts came close to a perfect score. Lazuka said it's hard to get a perfect 10, but they got a 9.9 and were very close to a 10. Rose-Daris said it's going to be really fun that she's going to an entire different part of the world. Supan described the qualification as happy and exciting at the same time. Rine said she is focused on getting first place on floors at the Junior Olympics.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance lowers homeowners rates by 5.6% statewide
cards.teaser: Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said customers are seeing the impact of the rate decreases. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Burt DeVriese said all those savings are required to be passed along to customers, and Security First has been doing so.

Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, the deductible goes down 20 percent each year as long as the customer does not have a loss. Once a customer has a loss, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount. Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state. Burt DeVriese said Security First is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292.

cards.headline: Court hearing scheduled on challenge to Fishback's gubernatorial eligibility
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback faces a ballot challenge alleging he does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors.
cards.body:
Lt. Gov. Jay Collins is challenging the candidacy of Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassee to address the eligibility challenge. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. Because ballots have already been printed for the July 18 primary, the judge said a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots.

The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Fishback denies being antisemitic and says the spending shows Republican establishment figures are concerned about his campaign. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Fishback at 8% support in the Republican gubernatorial primary, behind U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds at 48% and Collins at 9%.

cards.headline: DeSantis remains neutral as Trump endorses Donalds in governor race
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump has endorsed Byron Donalds in the Republican primary for governor, while Gov. Ron DeSantis has remained publicly neutral despite appointing Jay Collins as lieutenant governor.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump has endorsed U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds in Florida's Republican primary for governor. Gov. Ron DeSantis, who appointed Jay Collins as lieutenant governor in August 2025, has remained publicly neutral in the primary contest. Collins has not received an endorsement from DeSantis despite serving as his lieutenant governor. During a Thursday campaign call, Collins positioned himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds, rejected claims of tension between his campaign and staff inside the governor's office, and urged former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner to leave the race. Collins defended his support for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and law enforcement.

The available polling shows Collins has considerable ground to make up against Donalds. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48%, followed by Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8% and Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Donalds also holds a major financial advantage, with his campaign announcing more than $90 million raised across his campaign operation. Recent reports placed Collins' available resources at a fraction of that amount.

cards.headline: Florida homeowners pay highest average insurance premium in nation at $8,292
cards.teaser: Online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state and is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida, according to company president Melissa Burt DeVriese.

Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, every year the deductible goes down 20 percent as long as the customer doesn't have a loss. Once a loss occurs, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount. Premiums in South Florida generally run high, and online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292. State insurance regulators said that with more companies and more competition, homeowners should seek better premiums by shopping around.

cards.headline: Democratic poll shows Jolly ahead of Donalds in Florida general election matchup
cards.teaser: A June survey commissioned by a Democratic group showed David Jolly leading Byron Donalds 47% to 42% among registered voters and 49% to 43% among likely voters.
cards.body:
Jolly has pointed to a June Change Research survey commissioned by Freedom Project USA, a group aligned with Democrats, that showed him ahead of Donalds. The poll found Jolly leading 47% to 42% among registered voters and 49% to 43% among likely voters. However, respondents were shown prepared descriptions of both candidates before being asked whom they supported, making the results less directly comparable to a standard, unprompted ballot test. The survey reported a margin of error of 2.8 percentage points. Other polling has shown Donalds ahead of Jolly, and an average compiled earlier this summer placed Donalds narrowly in front.

Donalds continues to hold a commanding advantage in Republican polling and fundraising, while Jolly has consolidated support in the Democratic contest. A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48%, followed by Collins at 9%, businessman James Fishback at 8% and former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner at 4%. About 26% of respondents remained undecided. Lt. Gov. Jay Collins used a Thursday campaign call to argue Donalds could struggle in a general election, though Collins trails the congressman in polling, money and endorsements. Florida's voter registration deadline is July 20, with the primary set for August 18.

hero.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway following Hurricane Milton tornado damage
hero.body:
Demolition has begun at Murray Middle School in Martin County as part of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay.

Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. The school district has implemented safety measures during the construction process, with barriers already placed around the work zone to keep students out of the area. The district aims to complete the renovations by December 2027.

Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, explained that the hurricane damage affected a project that was already in the planning stages. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," Gernaine said. "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on."

The combination of planned improvements and tornado recovery has created an extensive construction project at the school. District officials said parents can be assured their students will be safe during the construction period. The reconstruction of buildings 18, 10, and nine will proceed alongside the previously planned additions to the campus. The lengthy timeline reflects the scope of work needed to both repair the storm damage and complete the facility upgrades that had been scheduled before Hurricane Milton struck the area.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
hero.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
hero.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

hero.headline: JetBlue ending direct flights from Vero Beach to New York JFK in September
hero.teaser: JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airlin
hero.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end September 9, just nine months after the route began operating. JetBlue told WPTV that demand for the new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped. The carrier will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route, and all affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. The optimism surrounding the launch contrasted sharply with the route's short lifespan, as the service failed to attract sufficient passenger numbers to remain viable.

Vero Beach Regional Airport has worked to expand its commercial service in recent years, with JetBlue's Boston route continuing to serve travelers seeking alternatives to larger South Florida airports. The Boston service remains operational and provides ongoing connectivity for the region. However, the loss of the JFK route represents a setback for efforts to increase air service options at the smaller regional airport. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The airline's statement indicated that all affected customers would receive full refunds for their cancelled flights as the carrier winds down operations on the route over the coming weeks. The decision to discontinue the JFK service comes as airlines continue to evaluate route profitability and adjust their schedules based on passenger demand patterns.
